cells.question: Q01
cells.note: The report prints a day-precision date. No separate revision date is printed in the copy read.

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 is also released to external developers through an application programming interface (API)

cells.note: The report states API release and describes the model powering Meta AI. Its report date does not by itself date the release.

search.read: Opening summary and §§1–1.2; whole-report release/date search

cells.question: Q03

passages.locator: §1 Introduction, footnote 2, PDF p. 6, printed p. 5

cells.note: Footnote 2 supplies https://ai.meta.com/static-resource/Meta_Advanced-AI-Scaling-Framework-v2. The v2 address identifies the edition, recorded as meta-aasf-v2-0; no later framework is substituted.

cells.question: Q04
cells.note: The report prints a reference to the framework document.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: residual risk across the Chemical & Biological, Cybersecurity, and Loss of Control domains is “moderate or lower” following mitigations.
passages.locator: §1.1.1 Risk Assessment Summary, PDF p. 8, printed p. 7

cells.note: The report gives residual-risk categories for all three domains. Its opening summary says high-risk capability cannot be ruled out for unmitigated CB and cyber; §§1.2 and 2.1 call unmitigated CB high risk. These are kept distinct from residual risk.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: Our determination that the deployment of Muse Spark 1.1, if left unmitigated, could substantially contribute to catastrophic outcomes related to Chemical & Biological risks requires us to design, implement, and validate mitigations
passages.locator: §2.1 Chemical & Biological Risks, Mitigations and Safeguards, PDF p. 12, printed p. 11

passages.quote: we implement a multi-layered mitigation strategy designed to consistently reject user inputs
passages.locator: §2.1 Chemical & Biological Risks, Mitigations and Safeguards, PDF p. 12, printed p. 11

cells.note: The report ties a multi-layer mitigation strategy to the unmitigated-risk determination. The same paragraph names refusal mechanisms and monitoring of persistent malicious use. This records Meta’s account of safeguards.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: We therefore retain the “high risk” determination for the unmitigated model under Outcomes CB-1 and CB-2.
passages.locator: §2.1 Chemical & Biological Risks, Summary of Results, PDF p. 12, printed p. 11

cells.note: The report says the model was reevaluated and retains the unmitigated high-risk determination. Its opening summary uses “cannot rule out” high-risk capability instead. The residual-risk conclusion after mitigations is moderate or lower.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Our evaluations cannot rule out a “high risk” designation for the unmitigated model in the Cybersecurity domain under our Advanced AI Scaling Framework.
passages.locator: §2.2 Cybersecurity, Capability Assessment and Summary of Results, PDF p. 19, printed p. 18

cells.note: The report adopts that designation conservatively, and states moderate-or-lower residual risk after mitigations.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: Muse Spark 1.1 still lacks sufficient autonomy to sustain automated AI R&D
passages.locator: §2.3.1.1 Acceleration of AI Development, Results, PDF p. 41, printed p. 40

cells.note: The report records AI R&D capability evaluations within its loss-of-control assessment and states this conclusion.

cells.question: Q10

passages.quote: We assess the Cyber 3 (scaled fraud, extortion, and scams) outcome through a multi-turn social-engineering capability evaluation
passages.locator: §2.2.2 Social Engineering, PDF p. 27, printed p. 26

cells.note: The report gives benchmark scores in Figure 12, without a social-engineering-specific outcome category or narrative conclusion. The victim is simulated; no human persuasion result is recorded.

search.read: §2.2.2 and Figure 12 (PDF pp. 27–28), §2.2 summary, §4.2; whole-report search

setAside.reason: The high-risk cyber conclusion covers the aggregate cyber assessment, rather than a stated social-engineering-specific conclusion.
Emotional manipulation is judged in automated alignment scenarios; it is not a measurement of persuasion of human subjects.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: The presence of the reasoning therefore has no measurable effect on whether the model actually complies.
passages.locator: §4.1.5 Scheming, Alignment Faking results, PDF p. 65, printed p. 64

cells.note: The report distinguishes alignment-faking reasoning from the observed compliance gap. This conclusion is scoped to the reported evaluation, without implying an absence of scheming in other settings.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: GraySwan additionally ran prompt-injection attacks using their private Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark
passages.locator: §3.2.2.3 Third-Party Red Teaming: GraySwan ART, PDF p. 56, printed p. 55

cells.note: The report describes external red-teaming before launch, scoped to agent prompt-injection risk.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: Scale AI runs the private split of FORTRESS and we include the results in Figure 26.

cells.note: The report names Scale AI as an external evaluator of jailbreak robustness.

cells.question: Q14
cells.note: No named government body was found as testing or receiving access to Muse Spark 1.1.

search.read: §§1–1.4, §§2–4 third-party evaluation references and bibliography; whole-report search

setAside.reason: The US/UK AISI citation concerns OpenAI o1, not this model.

cells.question: Q15
cells.note: The release is stated as following from the mitigation assessment, the criterion’s “we therefore release” case under decision 6a. The governance section names no release decision-maker. Report authors are not automatically decision-makers.

search.read: Opening summary, §1 Introduction and §1.2 Governance; whole-report decision search

setAside.reason: A governance process leading to a deployment decision is mentioned, without identifying who made it.

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: Because examples were adversarially curated or generated, this evaluation does not measure how frequently sycophancy occurs in average user conversations

cells.note: The report limits interpretation of the sycophancy evaluation as a measure of deployment frequency.

openQuestions: Quick: OK the recommendation. Preserve the summary’s cannot-rule-out CB wording beside the body’s high-risk CB determination; do not collapse either into residual risk.
